title: Regional traffic quarantine and KV consistency notes
summary: Working notes for executing a regional traffic quarantine when a region shows KV cache divergence or persistent edge failures. Focus is on isolating the region (quarantine), ensuring KV cache state parity for warm-standby reattachment, and minimizing global impact during staged evacuation or partial isolation.
incident_timeline: T+00:00 - Multiple edge clusters in eu-west-1 reported elevated 5xx from the router layer; synthetic checks failing 30% of requests.
T+00:12 - Alert: ingestion lag for KV cache updates (kv-sync lag > 2s) and a spike in stale-cache hits observed.
T+00:26 - Operator note: control-plane still reachable from other regions; some kms calls from eu-west-1 timing out intermittently.
T+00:40 - Decision: start traffic quarantine experiment on a small shard (10%) to validate rollback/failover mechanics.
T+01:05 - Quarantine successful for shard; observed drop in global error rate. Decided to scale to 50% quarantine while pre-seeding KV for warm-standby.
T+02:30 - KV epoch mismatch detected between eu-west-1 and preseed cluster -> paused further quarantine expansion. Began focused KV reconciliation steps.
T+04:10 - Reconciliation plan executed (log replay + controlled rebootstrap). eu-west-1 moved to warm-standby with DNS low TTL and 0 weight for production traffic.
T+06:00 - Incident declared mitigated. Follow-ups and postmortem items created.
T+???: - Unknown: small fraction of clients with long-lived connections retried into quarantined region; follow-up for client-side retry policies opened (SRE-1430).
immediate_actions: Open incident channel and tag on-call: #sre-ops, paging SRE on-call.
Set global alert to suppress noisy heartbeats for the affected region (avoid operator fatigue).
Set eu-west-1 routing weight to 0 for API route sets using traffic-router (staged ramp down for session draining).
Lower DNS TTL for region edge endpoints to 30s (if currently > 60s) to speed client redirection.
Pre-seed warm-standby KV cache from primary via kv-replay tool (dry-run first).
Enable read-only fallback mode for eu-west-1 to prevent cache writes until reconciliation completes.
operator_commands:
# check router weights
trafficctl get-weights --route api-main

# set weight to 0 for eu-west-1 (graceful drain)
trafficctl set-weight --route api-main --region eu-west-1 --weight 0 --drain 120

# lower DNS TTL via infra-dns tool
infra-dns update --zone edge.prod --record *.eu-west-1 --ttl 30

# inspect kv sync lag
kvtool status --region eu-west-1 --metric sync_lag_seconds

# preseed kv cache to standby node (dry-run)
kvtool preseed --from region-us-west-2 --to eu-west-1 --dry-run

# force-roll kv epoch if reconciliation succeeded
kvtool rotate-epoch --region eu-west-1 --confirm

# view active long-lived connections by nat bin
netdiag conn-list --region eu-west-1 --filter long-lived

# set region to read-only mode at app layer
infractl set-config --region eu-west-1 --service api --key write_mode --value read-only
telemetry_checks: error-rate (5xx) by region: expect drop in global error-rate after quarantine begins
kv-sync-lag histogram: < 200ms target for warm-standby preseed
cache-hit-ratio: monitor for unintended cache stampedes in fallback regions
client-retry distribution: ensure retries are not beating quarantine (observe retry-origin headers)
latency p99 for remaining regions: ensure no adverse impact from traffic redistribution
edge-connection-drop-rate: watch for connection churn when TTL lowered
k8s-pod-restarts in eu-west-1: could indicate broader instability beyond router layer
playbook_steps: 1) Initial triage: confirm control-plane reachability and isolate the fault domain (router, kv, or infra).
2) Small-scale quarantine: move 5-10% of traffic for a single route off eu-west-1 to validate rollback behavior (use trafficctl with drain window).
3) Preseed KV: if eviction or divergence suspected, run kvtool preseed to warm standby nodes; validate checksums & epoch alignment.
4) Scale quarantine: if small-scale passes, increase to 50% with continuous telemetry checks. Do not fully evacuate until KV epoch parity is confirmed.
5) Full quarantine (if required): set region weights to 0, enforce read-only, and set DNS to low TTL. Coordinate with platform teams to pause automated deploys in that region.
6) Recovery prep: once KV reconciliation is validated and upper-layer health checks green, reintroduce traffic with a canary (start 1-5% and ramp with monitoring).
7) Post-incident: collect runbooks, update playbook with specifics (what failed, effective drain time, TTL/dns caveats).
fallthrough_behaviors: If dns propagation is slower than expected: use IP-based routing overrides for internal clients (traffic-router allowlist for internal subnets).
If warm-standby preseed fails due to bandwidth: shift to a metadata-only reconciliation (epoch + tombstones) before full log replay.
If clients keep retrying into quarantined region: increase client-side retry-backoff in API gateway or issue temporary 429 with Retry-After header at edge to force backoff.
If kvtool reports conflicting epochs that can't be auto-merged: escalate to Applied ML / platform owner (kv-sync team) for manual merge tooling.
postmortem_notes: Root cause summary (working): intermittent control-plane auth latencies in eu-west-1 causing sporadic kv update failures and router mis-routes.
What went well: small-scale quarantine validated our rollback mechanics and prevented global error amplification.
What went wrong: we expanded quarantine before kv epoch parity was fully validated; this caused additional client retries into the quarantined region.
Telemetry gaps: need better visibility into client retry origin header and long-lived connection telemetry aggregated by region.
Runbook gaps: no quick operator command existed to downgrade client retry policies globally; added action item to implement infractl toggle.
followups: SRE-1428: build infractl toggle for global client-retry-backoff (owner: Marco, due 2025-03-15)
SRE-1430: add long-lived connection tagging to synthetic checks and dashboard (owner: Evelyn, due 2025-03-01)
PR-88: traffic-router change to support per-shard drain windows (review requested)
Confluence update: append this quarantine checklist to the main failover playbook and include command snippets.
unanswered_questions: Why did kv-sync lag spike concurrently with router 5xx? hypothesis: control-plane auth timeouts; needs trace-level correlation.
Do certain client SDK versions ignore DNS TTL and keep sticky IPs? need to audit client libraries for DNS caching behavior.
Should we adopt a default read-only fallback for all warm-standby regions? trade-offs: consistency vs availability for writes.
